verses.1: After these things, when Ahşverosh, the king, remembered Vashti and what she had done, and what was imposed upon her.
verses.2: And the young men of the king’s service said, “Let them ask the king for young girls with good looks.”
verses.3: And the king will appoint officials in all the provinces of his kingdom. He will bring forth every young girl who is beautiful to the royal palace, to the women’s quarters, and to the hands of King Sirus, who is in charge of the women. He will also give them gifts as rewards.
verses.4: And the girl who pleased the king’s eyes will reign under Vashti. And it pleased the king’s eyes, so he did as she requested.
verses.5: There was a Jewish man in Shushan, the capital city. His name was Mordechai, son of Yair, son of Shimei, son of Kish. He was a man from the right side.
verses.6: The one who was exiled from Jerusalem, along with the exile that you brought upon Jehoshaphat, king of Judah. The one who was exiled by Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.
verses.7: And Esther was born. She was the daughter of her father’s sister, since she had no father or mother. The young girl was beautiful and attractive in appearance. After her father and mother died, Mordecai took her as his daughter.
verses.8: And when she heard the king’s words and his commands, she rushed with many young girls to the royal palace. Esther was taken to the king’s court, where Hagar, the keeper of the women, took her away.
verses.9: The girl’s beauty captivated his eyes. He showed her kindness in front of her. He arranged her hair and makeup so that she could be given to him. And he took seven other beautiful girls from the king’s palace and arranged them in a better place to live with the women.
verses.10: Ester did not tell her people and her mother about it, because Mordecai had ordered her not to do so.
verses.11: And every day, Mordecai went before the women’s house to find out whether Esther was safe and what was happening with her.
verses.12: And when two young women came to come before King Ahšweros, it was according to the law of women: two twelve months had passed since their puberty. This is because their menstrual periods lasted for six months during the summer season, and six months during the winter season.
verses.13: And in this manner, the young woman came before the king, with everything that she had to say. She asked to be allowed to enter the king’s palace along with her.
verses.14: In the morning, she came; in the evening, she returned to the house of the women. She was given to Saagaz Sris, the king’s concubine. She would not enter the king’s palace again, unless the king desired her. Then she would be called by that name.
verses.15: And when Esther, the daughter of Abihail, arrived, her father Mordecai did not ask for anything in exchange for bringing her before the king. Instead, he simply said, “Let the king keep the women safe.” And Esther was accepted by all who saw her.
verses.16: And Esther went to the king, Ahasuerus, to his palace. It was the fifth month of his reign; that year was the seventh year of his reign.
verses.17: The king loved Esther more than any other woman. He showed him kindness and favor from all around. He placed her on the throne as his queen. She ruled over the land for seven years.
verses.18: And the king made a great feast for all his servants and ministers. He also gave Esther a place to sit at the table. And he appointed someone to serve at the king’s side.
verses.19: And in the second time, he will be raised from the dead; and Mordecai will sit in the gate of the king.
verses.20: Ester does not remember her homeland and her people, as Mordecai commanded her to do. Ester acts according to what Mordecai told her to do.
verses.21: In those days, Mordecai sat in the king’s court. He was angry with Haman and the two officers of the king. They tried to get Haman to attack King Ahaziah.
verses.22: And Mordecai heard about this. He told Esther, the queen. Esther said to the king in Mordecai’s name:
verses.23: He asked for that matter to be recorded. He found it, and they both were hanged from the trees. Then he wrote down their names in the book of records for the king’s use.
